chunks: Al-Sadiq عليه السلام said to ʿAmmār ibn Mūsā al-Sābāṭī: “O ʿAmmār, you are a man of much wealth.”

He said, “Yes, may I be your ransom.” He said: “Then do you render the zakat which Allah has made obligatory upon you?” He said, “Yes.” He said: “Then do you give the known right from your wealth?” He said, “Yes.” He said: “Then do you maintain your kinship ties?” He said, “Yes.” He said: “Then do you keep ties with your brothers?” He said, “Yes.”

So he said: “O ʿAmmār, wealth perishes, the body wears out, and deeds remain; and the Reckoner is Living and does not die. O ʿAmmār, indeed, whatever you have sent ahead will never outstrip you, and whatever you have left behind will never catch up with you.”

key_terms.إِخْوَانَكَ: your brothers, meaning fellow believers or close associates
key_terms.الدَّيَّانَ: the Reckoner, Allah, who judges and requites
key_terms.الزَّكَاةِ: the obligatory alms-tax due upon qualifying wealth
key_terms.الْحَقَّ الْمَعْلُومَ: the recognized due taken from wealth for others
key_terms.الْمَالَ: wealth or property that is temporary and perishable

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام teach about wealth, zakat, and deeds that remain for the Hereafter?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that material wealth is temporary, while righteous deeds endure before Allah. Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام links financial obligations, charity, and maintaining ties of kinship and brotherhood to a believer’s enduring provision for the Hereafter.
